_comment_family: Poppins Regular, from the Google Fonts repository (ofl/poppins), under
the SIL Open Font License like the other Google faces in fonts/.
Poppins ships as eighteen cuts - nine weights and their italics - and
every one of them carries 'Poppins' as name ID 1, with the cut in the
subfamily. Only the Regular is in this folder, so a request for
'Poppins' inside the app can only reach this file: the FontFace
registered from this JSON is the one face under that family the
browser holds, at the weight the canvas asks for. That is why the
family is declared plainly here rather than as a full name the way
syne-regular.json has to - there is no second cut in the app for the
request to land on.
The danger is on the machine instead, and it is handled in `local`
below: a designer's PC may well have the whole family installed.
Weight 400, the file's own usWeightClass. It is a static cut, not an
instance of a variable font - there is no fvar table - so nothing is
interpolated, and asking for 400 asks for exactly these outlines.
Unlike the Bebas it is set beside, Poppins has a real lower case. The
preset uppercases every caption under the Snapchat heading (see
`uppercase` in presets/snapchat-caption.json), so a picked word is in
Poppins' capitals like the rest of the block.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css. This face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes -
nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The PostScript name first, then the full name. Both name this one
cut, so a machine answering to either is answering with this file.
'Poppins' on its own is deliberately absent: it is the name all
eighteen cuts answer to, and a machine with the family installed
could hand back the Bold or the Light under it.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, never a design choice - a block laid out against
the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely different, which is
what fontguard exists to catch before anything is drawn.
Chosen all the same, and written as the opposite of the block's
stack. This is the HIGHLIGHT face on a channel set in Bebas Neue
Cyrillic (see conspiracy-central), so it falls through the
ordinary-width sans faces Windows can be relied on to have, and
never through Anton or Impact: a substitute in the block's condensed
register would take away the one thing that sets a picked word
